1. Heard Ms. Amrita Ajmera, learned advocate for the petitioners - original claimants.
Mr. Sunil Parikh, learned advocate has entered his appearance on behalf of the respondent no.1- Insurance Company.

2. The present petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking issuance of writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ, direction or order for quashing and setting aside the order dated 09.03.2015 passed below Exh.11 in Execution Petition No.14 of 2013.

Further direction is also sought to hold the present petitioners entitled to interest at the rate of 15% from the date on Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99536062/

3. In order to appreciate the controversy involved, appropriate would be to consider the relevant dates.
The petitioners are heirs of one Deepak Anantrai Sheth who had unfortunately expired in motor vehicle accident.

The petitioners have therefore, approached the Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal, Navsari by preferring the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "Act, 1988"), which was registered as MACP No.532 of 1987.

Pending the claim petition,
the same was transferred to the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Valsad.

The Tribunal was pleased to partly allowed the claim petition thereby holding the present petitioners entitled to total amount of compensation of Rs.3,82,705/- with interest at the rate of 15% from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realization.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgment and award, the respondent no.1 - Insurance Company had approached in appeal before this Court under Section 173 of the Act, 1988.
The First Appeal No.6254 of 1995 was thus registered on 15.08.1995.
Along with appeal, an application for stay was also preferred by the respondent - Insurance Company.

At the stage of admission hearing of the appeal and aforesaid application for stay, this Court upon appreciation of the facts of the case and impugned judgment NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined and award vide order dated 28.02.1996 was pleased to grant interim relief thereby staying the execution, implementation and operation of the impugned judgment and award dated 19.7.1995 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Valsad in MACP No.532 of 1987 pending the final hearing of the appeal on condition of deposit of the awarded amount with interest and costs with the concerned Tribunal within a period of six weeks thereafter.
In terms of the aforesaid direction, the respondent Insurance Company had deposited total amount of Rs.8,55,981/- on24.4.1996.
The appeal was thereafter heard finally and was dismissed by order dated 09.12.2011.
The original claimants had approached the Tribunal seeking withdrawal of the aforesaid deposited awarded amount of Rs.8,55,981/- which was later on realized by the petitioner on 14.6.2013.

The petitioners, thus, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the deficit amount of award had preferred execution application before the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal specifically contending that they were entitled to the deficit amount of compensation, which was computed as Rs.3,82,075/- with interest at the rate of 15% as awarded by the Tribunal by judgment and award dated 27.7.1995 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in claim petition along with interest at the rate of 15% from the date of filing of such application till its realisation i.e. for the period from 3 rd September 1987 to 14th June 2013.

The execution application was heard by the Tribunal and by order dated 9 th March 2015 has partly rejected the Execution Application thereby directing the respondent Insurance Company to pay further amount to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined tune of RS.1,26,940/-.

Thus, by impugned order the Tribunal has not entertained the claim of the original claimants with regard to the entitlement of the deficit amount with 15% interest from the date of the filing of original claim petition till its actual realisation.
Hence, present petition at the instance of the petitioners -original claimants.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Ms. Amrita Ajmera appearing for the petitioners has invited my attention to the aforesaid dates.

At the outset, learned advocate has drawn my attention to the operative part of the judgement and award dated 12 th July 1995 passed by the Tribunal in the original claim proceedings to point out that the claimants were held entitled to total amount of compensation of Rs.3,82,705/-
with interest at the rate of 15% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realisation.
She has further invited my attention to the findings and reasons assigned by the learned Single Judge of this court while deciding the appeal finally vide order dated 9th December 2011.

4.1. Referring to the relevant operative part of the aforesaid order, learned advocate has contended that the appeal of the respondent Insurance Company was dismissed by observing that the same was devoid of any merits.
The Court has therefore concluded that no interference was called for and the reasoning adopted by the Tribunal was just and proper.

She had therefore submitted that the specific directions of the Tribunal of awarding interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realisation on the total amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined compensation has been upheld by this Court in the substantive appeal preferred by the respondent Insurance Company.

Despite aforesaid settled position, the Executing Court while hearing the Execution Petition has refused to entertain the claim of the present petitioners - original claimants as regards to the deficit amount of award being not deposited and the interest accrued thereon from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realization.

4.2. The attention of this Court was invited to the relevant calculation proposed in the Execution Petition at page 17.
4.3.
Learned advocate has thereafter referred to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while partly not entertaining the claim of the petitioners in the execution proceedings.
She has submitted that the Tribunal ignored the legal principles while examining the execution petition that the Executing Court cannot beyond the decree.

She has submitted that the having noted the relevant dates and the amount deposited, the Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that the amount was not actually realised by the original claimants -petitioners as it was deposited with the concerned Tribunal and was not actually paid to the original claimants.
She has further submitted that the stay order was obtained by the Insurance Company in the pending appeal.
In such circumstances, the execution proceedings could not proceed further.

Once the appeal was dismissed, the order passed by the Tribunal had merged into the order of this Court and therefore the interest to be accrued during the interregnum NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED:
10/07/2025 undefined period of appeal was required to be paid to the claimants.
4.4. The reliance was placed on the decision of this Court in the case of State of Gujarat versus Gangaji Ramji reported in 1996(1) GLH 22 (UJ).

The attention of this court was also invited to the judgment of Delhi High Court in the case of State of Haryana versus KL, Pasricha and Ors reported in I (2000) ACC 354, wherein in similar set of facts, the Court held that if a stay is obtained by the opposite party and the deposit amount is not released, then the claimants shall be entitled to interest on the deposited amount from the date of petition till its actual realization.
4.6.

sentences.text: The Executing Court cannot go beyond the decree.
Even if the ambiguity arises in the decree with regard to material aspects, then it becomes the bounden duty of the Court to interpret the decree in the process of giving a true fact to the decree.

4.7. She has therefore submitted that the Tribunal had failed to exercise its jurisdiciton and has therefore urged this court to quash and set aside the order dated 9 th March 2015 passed by the Tribunal below Exhibit 11 to the extent it refused to entertain the claim of the petitioners in not extending the interest for the interregnum period of appeal on the deficit amount.
5. Mr. Sunil B. Parikh, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent no.1 Insurance Company has forcefully objected to the aforesaid submissions of learned advocate for the petitioners.
5.1. The attention of this Court was invited to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal.
Learned advocate has pointed out that the appeal was preferred in the month of August 1995.
At that stage an amount of Rs.25,000/- was deposited towards the statutory amount to be deposited at the stage of filing of appeal.
He had further pointed out that in fact a caveat was filed by the claimants through the practicing advocate of the High Court.

He has further invited NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined my attention to the order of 20 th February 1996 passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench in application for stay.
Pursuant to the aforesaid directions, learned Advocate has submitted that the entire award amount with interest and cost was deposited on 24th April 1996, which was to the tune of Rs.8,55,980/-.

He has therefore submitted that in fact in absence of the statutory amount deposited of Rs.25,000 at the stage of filing of appeal being not transferred to the concerned Tribunal, the Tribunal had unnecessarily fixed the liability of the Insurance Company to pay the interest on the deficit amount as noticed by the Tribunal while passing the impugned order below Exh.11.
5.2.

Learned advocate had further pointed out that at the stage of deposit of the amount with the concerned Tribunal, the endorsement of the lawyer representing the original claimants was taken on the pursis.

By referring to aforesaid circumstances, learned advocate had pointed out that the claimants were therefore in knowledge of the fact of deposit of the award amount with the Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99536062/

He had further pointed out that since the stay was operating all throughout pending the appeal i.e. from the February 1996 till the appeal was decided in the year 2011, no fault can be found with the respondent Insurance Company and no liability arises with regard to the amount of interest to be approved on such amount as claimed by the claimants.

According to him, the entire award amount with proportionate cost has been deposited way back in the year 1996 and therefore, has urged this court to not to entertain the present petition or to award the interest on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined award amount till the disposal of the appeal.

6. Considering the controversy raised in the present petition, it would be appropriate to look into the relevant provisions of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which reads as under:
"21. Execution of Decrees and Orders Payment under Decree 1. Modes of paying money under decree.-
(1) All money, payable under a decree shall be paid as follows, namely:-
(a) by deposit into the court whose duty it is to execute the decree, or sent to that Court by postal money order or through a bank; or (b) out of Court, to the decree-holder by postal money order or through a bank or by any other mode wherein payment is evidenced in writing; or (c) otherwise, as the Court which made the decree, directs.

(2) Where any payments is made under clause (a) or clause (c) of sub-rule (1), the judgment-debtor shall give notice thereof to the decree-holder either through the Court or directly to him by registered post, acknowledgment due.

entities.text: Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (4) On any amount paid under clause (a) or clause (c) of sub-rule (1), interest, if any, shall cease to run from the date of service of the notice referred to in sub-rule (2).
( 5) On any amount paid under clause (b) of sub-rule (1), interest, if any, shall cease to run from the date of such payment:

Provided that, where the decree-holder refuses to accept the postal money order or payment through a bank, interest shall cease to run from the date on which the money was tendered to him, or where he avoids acceptance of the postal money order or payment through bank, interest shall cease to run from the date on which the money would have been tendered to him in the ordinary course of business of the postal authorities or the bank, as the case may be.]"
7. On plain reading of the aforesaid provision, in my view it clarifies the proposition of law on this point.

Sub-Rule 4 of Order XXI provides that payment of amount under clause (a) or clause (c) of sub-rule (1), interest, if any, shall cease to run from the date of service of notice referred to in sub-rule (2), which requires the judgment debtor to give notice of depositing amount in the executing Court to the decree holder either through the Court or directly to him by Registered Post Acknowledgement Dues.

Thus, to claim satisfaction of the decree, the decree holder has to first deposit the amount in the executing Court in terms of clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of Order XXI or has to pay decreetal amount to the decree holder by postal money or through bank or by any other mode, wherein the payment is evidence in writing or otherwise as the Court which made the decree directs.

entities.text: clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of Order XXI
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: If the decreed NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined amount is deposited in terms of clause (a) and (c) of sub-rule (1), the judgment debtor is duty bound to give notice thereof to the decree holder.

Thus, the interest shall cease to run only on depositing the amount in terms of the aforesaid rules and further from the date of the service of notice referred to in sub-clause (2).
8. Having considered the aforesaid provisions, it would be appropriate to look into the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of P. Ramanathan Chettiar & others v. ORMPRM Ramanathan Chettiar, A.I.R. 1968, SC 1047.

sentences.text: The facts of the case suggest that the respondent father had made deposit of the amount with the father of the appellant, which was repayable with interest.
The demand was raised for repayment of the aforesaid deposited amount, which ultimately led to the filing of suit for recovery of the amount.
The trial Court upon appreciation of evidence decreed the suit.
The High Court confirmed the decree.
The dispute arose about the actual date when the stay of the execution of the decree was obtained.
The execution proceedings were filed.

The judgment debtor moved an application under the Madras Agriculture Relief Act for scaling down the decree Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99536062/
6 under Section 19(2) thereof.

sentences.text: The decree holder raised various objections thereto.
The aforesaid objections were turned down.
The appeal was preferred before the High Court.
The conflicting decisions of the High Court.
The question arose whether a judgment debtor who had not claimed relief under the Act before passing of the decree would do so subsequently.
The appeal was directed to be heard by a full NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined bench.

The High Court embraced the dispute arose in the process of hearing that there can be no doubt that on a deposit it may make the depositor incurred a liability, although the time for repayment would come only when a demand was made and the cause of action for the suit would arise on such demand.
The High Court in appeal, reversed the order of subordinate Judge by holding that the money entrusted was a deposit with a banker and was not payable until there was a demand for it.
The High Court also held that the provisions of Section 19(2) of the Act, 1988 waere not applicable and the decree was not liable to be scaled.

Before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the contention was raised by the respondent that the word "debt"implied pre existing loan and would not apply to a deposit and in terms of judgment, decree has been satisfied.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court allowed the appeal merely upholding the decision of subordinate Judge of the scaling drawn decree.
The Court in paragraphs 12 and 13 proceeded to examine the issue about entitlement of interest of the deposited amount.

It would be relevant to reproduce the observations which reads as under:
"12.On principle, it appears to us that the facts of a judgment- debtor's depositing a sum in court to purchase peace by way of stay of execution of the decree on terms that the decree- holder can draw it out on furnishing security, does not pass title to the money to the decree-holder.

He can if he likes take the money out in terms of the order; but so long as he does not do it, there is nothing to prevent the judgment- debtor from taking it out by furnishing other security, say, of immovable property,' if the court allows him to do so and on his losing the appeal putting the decretal amount in court in terms of Order 21 rule 1 C.P.C. in NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined satisfaction of the decree.
13. The real effect of deposit of money in court as was done in this case is to put the money beyond the reach of the parties pending the disposal of the appeal.

The decree- holder could only take it out on furnishing security which means that the payment was not in satisfaction of the decree and the security could be proceeded against by the judgment debtor in case of his success in the appeal.
Pending The determination of the same, it was beyond the reach of the judgment-debtor.

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court thus held that depositing the sum in the Court to obtain stay to the execution of the decree on the terms that the decree holder can draw it out on furnishing security is in effect an act of putting money beyond the reach of the parties pending disposal of the appeal because the decree holder could only take it out on furnishing the security, which means that the payment was not in satisfaction of the decree and the security can be proceeded against by the judgment debtor in case of his success in the appeal.

Thus, where the amount deposited is not unconditional and the decree holder is not free to withdarw it, there is no question of the stoppage Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99536062/
7 or interest after the deposit.
10.

sentences.text: The aforesaid decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court was followed by the Division Bench of the Delhi High Court in the case of Delhi Development Authority v. Bhai Sardar Singh and sons others reported in 2009 SCC online Del 519.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v. Bhai Sardar Singh and sons others reported in 2009 SCC online Del 519
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Division Bench held that the act of making payment to the decree holder under Rule (1) of Order XXI of CPC NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined would require a positive act on part of the judgment debtor and the payment made should be unconditional.
Accordingly, the Court held that the judgment debtor should deposit the amount before the executing Court and give notice to the decree holder to facilitate him to withdraw the amount.
Thus, it was held that the interest will not stop accruing if the amount awarded to the decree holder is deposited in the Court other than the executing Court.

The Court also observed that even if the amount is deposited in the executing Court, unless the notice contemplated by Sub-Rule (2) of Rule (1) of Order XXI is given, the judgment debtor's liability to pay interest does not cease.

entities.text: Sub-Rule (2) of Rule (1) of Order XXI
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 11. Considering the aforesaid legal principles in the facts of the case on hand, in my view mere deposit of the award amount with the Tribunal in terms of the directions of the appellate Court pending appeal would not amount to payment to the decree holder.

The insurance company could not shirk from its liability to make payment of the interest awarded by the Tribunal which was till the actual realisation of the awarded amount, on dismissed of the such appeal.

12. Having considered the aforesaid legal principles in light of the findings and reasons assigned by the executing Court, the executing Court has very casually and in superficial manner noted that there is no clarity in the directions of the High Court in the appeal and the claimants have not raised any dispute about interest in the appeal or before the Tribunal about the payment of interest which is in complete disregard NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/18665/2016 JUDGMENT DATED:
10/07/2025 undefined to the aforesaid legal position.
In the opinion of this Court, once the appeal was dismissed, the judgment of the Tribunal under challenge had got confirmed and it becomes enforceable the day on which the appeal was dismissed.
The stay operating all throughout in the pending appeal had got vacated.
The Tribunal had awarded interest to be paid till actual realisation of the award amount.
However, the executing Court has confined the determination of interest till the date of the deposit of the amount by the insurance company with the Tribunal which is on 24 th April, 1996.
In my view, the executing Court has failed to enforce the award in the terms of the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Since, there was no actual realisation of the award amount by the claimants on the date of the deposit.

In view of the aforesaid settled legal position,
because of the stay operating against the claimant on 24th April, 1996, the cause arose for the claimant to immediately seek enforcement of the judgment and award of the Tribunal on dismissal of such appeal and vacating of such stay.
13. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned order dated 9 th March, 2015 passed by the executing Court below Exh.11 is quashed and set aside.
The executing Court is directed to enforce the judgment in terms of the award drawn by the Tribunal.

The insurance company is thus directed to deposit the interest on the amount of compensation from the date of the deposit of the part of the Parulben Dipakkumar Sheth vs National Insurance Co. Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99536062/
8 amount of compensation that is from 24th April, 1996 till its actual realisation.
